title: Ordinary Engram exchange diagnostics: record frame-write to reply-decode timing
outcome: The host records, for each Engram control exchange, the exact frame boundary from frame write to reply receipt and decode, joined with the existing queueing, startup, binding, fence and worker-start timings, so a gated turn's admission time can be split into its Engram RPC portion and its TermAl portion during the w-7bc3 measurement window.
acceptance: ObservingTransport (or its existing owner) records a monotonic frame-write-to-reply-decode duration for every Engram control exchange, with SID, operation, attempt and frame identifiers that let it be correlated with Engram's phase and transaction traces. Recording is bounded, non-blocking, and never changes a request, a reply or a budget (TermAl dispatch 20 s and Engram frame 15 s stay unchanged).

The recorded exchange timing is joined with the existing binding, fence and worker-start timings in the same diagnostic record or report, so the Engram RPC share and the TermAl share of an admission are separable without inference.

Deterministic tests with an injected transport clock cover a normal exchange, a slow reply and a failed or undecodable reply, with no sleeps or synthetic load. The full gate passes on the exact committed tree with an independent review pair and no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
